title: Strict completion ignores review fragments changed after their last merge
observed_behavior: The strict evidence gate reconstructs and compares current finding and error fragments, but never loads current review fragments or proves that COVERAGE_MATRIX.jsonl is their deterministic merge. In an isolated Git repository, a current review fragment withdrew completion with blocked_with_reason while the matrix retained line_reviewed_no_findings; review_fragment_findings accepted the fragment and check_outputs(require_complete=True) still returned an empty finding list.
expected_invariant: A strict achieved-completion check must prove that the coverage matrix is the deterministic merge of all current valid review fragments, and must fail if any fragment is newer, divergent, blocked, missing from the matrix, or otherwise unmerged.
root_cause: Freshness reconciliation was added for finding and error ledgers and for worktree content during review merge, but the read-only strict check has no review-fragment-to-matrix reconciliation path.
failure_scenario: A worker corrects or withdraws a terminal review after the coordinator's last merge, marking the current fragment blocked or adding a finding. A later strict check reads only the stale terminal matrix and reports success, suppressing the current worker evidence.
evidence: Static evidence: evidence_ledger_findings lines 1599-1648 validates only finding and error fragments/central ledgers.
Static evidence: check_outputs lines 1664-1681 validates matrix shape/content plus evidence_ledger_findings but never calls load_review_fragments or reconstructs the merged matrix.

Adversarial evidence: strict_before_fragment=[], current_fragment_validation=[], and strict_after_current_fragment_withdraws_completion=[] while matrix_status=line_reviewed_no_findings and fragment_status=blocked_with_reason.
Test evidence: the hardened suite tests stale error-ledger freshness and pre-merge worktree drift, but no test changes a review fragment after a successful/current matrix state.
existing_safeguards: merge_review_ledgers validates baseline/current file identity before and after applying fragments, and strict checking validates source hashes plus current finding/error central artifacts.
safeguard_gap: Those checks protect a merge transaction and two evidence ledgers, but do not prove the matrix still represents the current review-fragment set at check time.
tests_missing: A post-merge review-fragment edit test that expects strict checking to reject a stale matrix.
Missing/duplicate/reordered review-fragment provenance tests against the central matrix.
A deterministic current-review-fragment digest or reconstruction assertion in the final proof gate.
recommended_remediation: Add a deterministic review-fragment preparation/reconstruction function for read-only checking, validate every fragment against the current baseline, compare all review-controlled fields with the matrix, and make --require-complete fail on any unmerged, missing, duplicate, invalid, or divergent fragment.
remediation_risk: medium: fragment freshness must coexist with intentionally staged review work and should distinguish an incomplete in-progress fragment from a current terminal proof without silently ignoring either.
validation_rung: Targeted unit tests plus isolated Git CLI flows for clean merge, post-merge edit, new fragment, removed fragment, blocked withdrawal, and finding/error-ID changes; strict checking must fail until remerge.
prior_audit_relationship: New hardening-gap finding discovered while re-reviewing the resolved stale-worktree merge defect W11-006; it concerns post-merge evidence freshness rather than worktree freshness during merge.

title: Normalization silently overwrites already-normalized historical finding links
observed_behavior: Both schemas accept optional historical_* arrays and also permit recognized historical IDs in the ordinary related/link arrays. During preparation, historical IDs moved from the ordinary array replace rather than merge with an existing historical array. Valid probe records containing CPA-2026-07-19-OLD in the historical array and FR-NEW in the ordinary array normalized aliases correctly but retained only FR-NEW, silently dropping CPA-2026-07-19-OLD in both finding and error outputs.
expected_invariant: Normalization must preserve the union of valid existing historical links and newly separated historical links, reject duplicates or conflicts deterministically, and never discard provenance from a schema-valid fragment.
root_cause: prepare_finding_records and prepare_error_records assign a newly derived historical list over the optional preexisting list instead of validating, unioning, de-duplicating, and stably ordering both sources.
failure_scenario: A worker updates a previously normalized record and adds another historical relationship in the ordinary compatibility field. Merge succeeds and central freshness checks accept the deterministic output, but an older cross-audit relationship disappears without an error or warning.
evidence: Static evidence: finding_record_findings and error_record_findings validate existing historical arrays as legal optional fields.
Static evidence: prepare_finding_records line 1119 and prepare_error_records line 1346 overwrite the historical field whenever newly separated IDs exist.

Adversarial evidence: finding alias/disposition normalized to medium/confirmed and error classification normalized to expected negative-path result, with zero validation issues, but each output historical array changed from the valid existing CPA ID plus FR ID to only [FR-NEW].
Test evidence: the 19-test suite has no preparation-output assertion for aliases combined with preexisting historical arrays.
existing_safeguards: Recognized historical ID formats are validated; current IDs are separated from historical IDs; legacy confidence, disposition, and error-classification aliases retain source_* provenance.
safeguard_gap: The historical arrays themselves have no merge-preservation rule, duplicate check, or test for mixed pre-normalized and compatibility inputs.
tests_present: Schema tests cover malformed errors and exact finding deduplication; isolated probing confirmed simple alias normalization works.
tests_missing: Mixed existing/new historical links for findings and errors.
Stable de-duplication and ordering of historical links.
A round-trip normalization test proving no relationship is lost across repeated merges.
recommended_remediation: Normalize historical links as a stable de-duplicated union of the optional historical array and recognized historical IDs removed from the ordinary array; reject overlaps or invalid values before writing, then validate the normalized record again.
remediation_risk: low: the change only preserves additional provenance, though deterministic ordering must remain stable for central-ledger freshness comparisons.
validation_rung: Targeted preparation and merge tests for finding/error aliases, current links, historical links in both input fields, duplicates, repeated normalization, and exact central output snapshots.
prior_audit_relationship: New normalization defect found while verifying the W11-005 and W11-007 hardening; the original findings did not cover mixed pre-normalized historical fields.

title: Parent-segment path aliases bypass exact root-cause deduplication and repository containment
observed_behavior: canonical_path normalizes separators and leading ./ but retains parent segments. Two otherwise identical findings using src/a.py and src/../src/a.py therefore receive different root-cause fingerprints. In an isolated repository both location checks resolved to the same current file, yet finding_record_findings returned no findings. The same root-join logic can resolve a sufficiently deep ../ path outside the repository if that external file exists.
expected_invariant: Finding locations must be canonical repository-relative paths contained under the audited root, and semantically identical path aliases must resolve to one identity before location validation and root-cause fingerprinting.
root_cause: Path canonicalization is lexical and does not reject parent segments or prove resolved containment; fingerprinting consumes that noncanonical lexical path while location validation joins it to root and follows filesystem resolution.
failure_scenario: Duplicate reports evade exact deduplication by spelling the same primary location with a parent-segment alias, or a malformed fragment cites an existing file outside the repository and passes the current-file check as audit evidence.
evidence: Static evidence: canonical_path lines 418-424 does not reject or collapse .. components.
Static evidence: finding_root_cause_fingerprint hashes the lexical canonical_path result at line 951.
Static evidence: finding_record_findings joins root/PurePosixPath(location_path) and calls is_file without a resolved-root containment check.
Adversarial evidence: canonical_1=src/a.py, canonical_2=src/../src/a.py, fingerprints_equal=false, and findings=[] for two identical-root-cause records referencing the same file.
Test evidence: the exact-duplicate test uses byte-identical normal paths and does not cover path aliases or traversal.
existing_safeguards: Paths use POSIX separators, fingerprints case-fold primary paths, line ranges are validated, and root-aware validation requires the joined location to be a current file.
safeguard_gap: No invariant forbids absolute/drive-like/parent-segment inputs or proves that the resolved location remains under the repository root before fingerprinting and reading it.
tests_missing: Parent-segment, absolute, drive-prefixed, UNC, repeated-separator, and case-alias location tests.
Resolved containment tests against an existing file outside the temporary repository.
Deduplication tests proving equivalent path spellings produce one fingerprint.
recommended_remediation: Introduce a strict repository-relative path validator for evidence records: reject absolute, drive/UNC, empty, dot, and parent components; resolve against root and require containment; use the validated normalized relative path for both fingerprints and location checks.
remediation_risk: medium: existing fragments containing tolerated noncanonical paths will need correction, and Windows case/drive semantics require deterministic tests.
validation_rung: Targeted path-identity and finding-schema tests on Windows-compatible path forms, isolated root-containment probes, and end-to-end finding merges demonstrating exact deduplication across equivalent spellings.
prior_audit_relationship: New bypass in the exact-fingerprint implementation added to resolve W11-007; the original implementation had no root-cause identity at all.

title: Paired audit artifacts publish partially and strict checking ignores a missing coverage mirror
observed_behavior: atomic_write_text safely replaces one file, but multi-artifact operations call it sequentially without a set-level commit. A synthetic second-write failure left FINDINGS.jsonl present while FINDINGS_REGISTER.md was absent. More critically, failure after COVERAGE_MATRIX.jsonl advanced left COVERAGE_MATRIX.csv absent; a subsequent check_outputs(require_complete=True) returned an empty finding list because coverage CSV and BASELINE.md are never checked.
expected_invariant: A merge/write operation must either publish its mutually-derived artifact set coherently or leave the prior set intact, and the strict proof gate must reject any missing or stale declared central mirror after interruption.
root_cause: Per-file temporary replacement is mistaken for transactionality across output sets, and strict validation reconstructs finding/error Markdown but has no equivalent deterministic presence/content checks for COVERAGE_MATRIX.csv or BASELINE.md.
failure_scenario: A disk, sharing, antivirus, or permission failure occurs between sequential replacements. The command returns nonzero but leaves the JSON coverage matrix terminal and its CSV mirror missing or stale; a later strict check reports clean, allowing incomplete evidence packaging to persist.
evidence: Static evidence: atomic_write_text provides fsync plus os.replace for one destination only.
Static evidence: merge_review_ledgers writes JSONL then CSV sequentially; write_outputs writes JSONL, CSV, then baseline sequentially.
Static evidence: check_outputs loads only COVERAGE_MATRIX.jsonl and never validates the CSV or baseline mirrors, unlike finding/error Markdown checks.
Adversarial evidence: synthetic finding-register failure produced jsonl_exists=true, markdown_exists=false.
Adversarial evidence: synthetic coverage-CSV failure produced matrix_status_after_failure=line_reviewed_no_findings, csv_exists=false, and strict_check_after_partial_publication=[].
existing_safeguards: Every individual output is built completely in the destination directory, flushed, fsynced, and atomically replaced; finding/error strict checks detect stale or missing rendered Markdown.
safeguard_gap: There is no output-set transaction, rollback, generation marker, or strict deterministic mirror check for coverage CSV/baseline artifacts.
tests_present: test_review_merge_refuses_stale_worktree_without_writing proves validation failure before the write phase leaves the matrix unchanged.
tests_missing: Injected failure on the second and third output replacement for every multi-artifact action.
Assertions that prior artifacts remain mutually consistent after publication failure.
Strict-check rejection of missing/stale COVERAGE_MATRIX.csv and BASELINE.md.
recommended_remediation: Stage every output in a generation directory or transaction manifest, validate the complete set, then atomically switch a generation pointer or implement rollback of already-replaced destinations. Independently make strict checking regenerate and byte-compare coverage CSV and validate baseline generation identity/presence.
remediation_risk: medium: true multi-file atomic publication needs a recoverable generation protocol on Windows; deterministic mirror checks are lower risk and should be added even if transactionality is staged later.
validation_rung: Fault-injection unit tests for each replacement boundary plus isolated CLI runs proving failed publication leaves a prior coherent generation and that strict checking rejects every missing/stale mirror.
prior_audit_relationship: New publication-integrity gap exposed while verifying the atomic stale-merge hardening for W11-006; the original finding concerned pre-write worktree freshness rather than multi-artifact failure.
